n2-licao-replicaset.titulo: The contract: always N apartments occupied
n2-licao-replicaset.enunciado:
A standalone pod (like the ones in the previous level) doesn’t come back if it’s deleted or if its node goes down: nobody asked for it to exist again. That’s what the ReplicaSet is for: a contract that says “I always want N identical pods.”

It has three parts in its spec:

  • replicas: how many;
  • selector: how it recognizes its own pods (by their labels);
  • template: the mold for each new pod (it’s a whole pod, minus the name).

The controller (Conceição, the inspector) compares all the time: fewer pods with those labels? Create one. More? Delete one. This is called reconciliation, and it’s the heart of Kubernetes.

The labels gotcha

The selector has to match the labels in the template: otherwise the ReplicaSet would create pods it doesn’t recognize itself, and Kubernetes rejects the YAML. And if you remove the label from a pod, the ReplicaSet “lets go” of that pod and creates another one in its place.

In practice, almost nobody creates a ReplicaSet by hand: the Deployment does it, coming up next.
n2-licao-replicaset.vidaReal: A contract that says “always 3 apartments occupied by the support team”: if one empties out, the management office fills another.
n2-licao-replicaset.limite: The contract only checks the tag on the door (the labels): a stranger’s apartment with the same tag counts as “part of the team.”

n2-licao-deployment.enunciado:
The Deployment manages ReplicaSets for you. When the template changes (another image, another variable), it creates a new ReplicaSet and moves the pods from the old one to the new one, a little at a time: the rolling update.

deployment/loja
└── replicaset/loja-6fdbb7c54b   (the suffix is a hash of the template)
    ├── pod/loja-6fdbb7c54b-8m9n7
    ├── pod/loja-6fdbb7c54b-9zjrw
    └── pod/loja-6fdbb7c54b-s742d

The everyday commands:

  • kubectl rollout status deploy/loja: follows the rollout until it’s done;
  • kubectl rollout history deploy/loja: the revisions (each old ReplicaSet is one);
  • kubectl rollout undo deploy/loja: goes back to the previous revision;
  • kubectl scale deploy/loja --replicas=5: changes the count (this does not create a revision).

To finish: apply the Deployment in the editor and look at the Deployment → ReplicaSet → Pods tree in the 🌳 Resources tab. Then, ⬆ Submit.
n2-licao-deployment.vidaReal: A renovation in stages: swap one apartment at a time, without closing the condo, and keep the old plans so you can undo it.
n2-licao-deployment.limite: In a real renovation someone checks that the new apartment turned out fine; here, without a readinessProbe (level 6), “the program started” already counts as ready.

n2-replicaset.enunciado:
The suporte (support) pod is standalone: if it goes down, it doesn’t come back. Replace the file with a ReplicaSet named suporte, with 3 replicas, that creates pods with the label app: suporte and the container web (nginx:1.27).

Then delete one of the pods and watch another one be born.
n2-replicaset.dica: kind: ReplicaSet (apps/v1) · spec: replicas, selector.matchLabels, template (metadata.labels + spec)
n2-replicaset.vidaReal: Trading the standalone apartment for a contract: “always 3 for support.”
n2-replicaset.limite: The ReplicaSet doesn’t change versions: changing the template doesn’t touch the pods that already exist. For that, use a Deployment.

testes.descricao: the pods are deleted and the contract recreates all 3

n2-deployment.enunciado: Turn the standalone loja pod into a Deployment named loja, with 3 replicas of the image kubelearn/loja:1.0 (label app: loja, port 8080).
n2-deployment.dica: kind: Deployment (apps/v1). The template is the pod from before, without metadata.name.
n2-deployment.vidaReal: The loja app stops being a standalone apartment and gets a contract with renovation in stages.
n2-deployment.limite: The Deployment takes care of the pods, not the data: if loja kept files inside the container, they’d vanish with every swap.
n2-deployment.comoSaber: kubectl get deploy loja shows 3/3, and the 🌳 Resources tab shows the tree.

testes.descricao: a pod goes down and the Deployment replaces it

n2-seletor-torto.titulo: The tag doesn’t match the contract
n2-seletor-torto.enunciado: This Deployment is rejected when you apply it. Read the error (and the 🏠 box under it) and fix the YAML, keeping the selector app: loja.
n2-seletor-torto.dica: spec.selector.matchLabels must be contained in spec.template.metadata.labels.
n2-seletor-torto.vidaReal: The contract says “team: loja,” but the door plates say “lojinha”: the inspector would never find the apartments.
n2-seletor-torto.limite: Here the doorman rejects the request right away; with ReplicaSets created by hand, a selector that’s too broad can “adopt” other people’s pods.

kubectl-escalar.titulo: Black Friday: more replicas from the terminal
kubectl-escalar.enunciado: Black Friday is here. Set deployment/loja to 5 replicas, using only the terminal (no YAML editing).
kubectl-escalar.vidaReal: Hiring temp staff for Black Friday: the contract goes from 3 to 5 occupied apartments, and the management office handles the rest.
kubectl-escalar.limite: Here you change the number by hand. To follow the demand on its own, there’s the HPA (level 6).

n2-autocura.titulo: It comes back on its own
n2-autocura.enunciado: Delete loja’s pods (one, or all at once with -l app=loja) and watch with kubectl get pods -w or in the 🗺️ Map tab. How many ready pods does loja have once everything calms down?
n2-autocura.vidaReal: An apartment under the contract emptied out? The inspector notices and fills another one right away.
n2-autocura.limite: The pod that comes back is a different one: new name, new IP, none of what was inside the old one.

deploy-rolling-sem-indisponibilidade.enunciado:
The loja app is running version 1.0 with 3 replicas. Version 1.1 just arrived.

  • switch the image to kubelearn/loja:1.1;
  • and make sure no pod becomes unavailable during the switch: maxUnavailable: 0 (it may create 1 extra pod at a time: maxSurge: 1).

After applying, follow along in the terminal: kubectl get pods -w or kubectl rollout status deploy/loja.
deploy-rolling-sem-indisponibilidade.dica: In spec: strategy → rollingUpdate → maxSurge: 1 and maxUnavailable: 0.
deploy-rolling-sem-indisponibilidade.vidaReal: A renovation in stages: open the new apartment, wait for it to be ready, and only then close the old one. The condo is never left without service.
deploy-rolling-sem-indisponibilidade.limite: In a real renovation someone checks that the apartment turned out fine. Here, without a readinessProbe, Kubernetes thinks “started” = “ready.”
deploy-rolling-sem-indisponibilidade.comoSaber: The 3 new pods become ready and, during the switch, there are never fewer than 3 pods serving.

n2-set-image.titulo: The new version from the terminal
n2-set-image.enunciado: Update loja to kubelearn/loja:1.1 from the terminal (the container is named loja) and follow it to the end with kubectl rollout status.
n2-set-image.vidaReal: Ordering the renovation over the intercom: “switch the loja apartments to model 1.1.”
n2-set-image.limite: A change made from the terminal doesn’t stay in the file: the next time the old YAML is applied, the version goes back to 1.0.

msgs.1: you followed it with rollout status

n2-rollback.enunciado:
Someone updated loja to 2.0-bugada (buggy). The new pod keeps crashing (check kubectl get pods and kubectl logs ... --previous), but the 3 old pods hold the fort, thanks to the rolling update.

Go back to the previous version.
n2-rollback.vidaReal: The new apartment turned out unlivable: the renovation stops and you order it undone, going back to the previous plans.
n2-rollback.limite: The rollback restores the pod template; if the new version had changed a database, that wouldn’t go back with it.
n2-rollback.comoSaber: All 3 loja pods are back on 1.0, with none in CrashLoopBackOff.

msgs.0: you undid it with rollout undo

n2-historico.enunciado: The loja app has already gone through three versions. The customer complained about the current one, and the previous one has a problem too. Check the history and go back to the revision from the store’s grand opening.
n2-historico.dica: kubectl rollout history ... and kubectl rollout undo ... --to-revision=N
n2-historico.vidaReal: Looking at the renovation log and choosing which old plans to go back to.
n2-historico.limite: The log only keeps the latest renovations (revisionHistoryLimit, 10 by default): older ones are deleted.

testes.descricao: loja is back to its grand opening

n2-change-cause.enunciado:
Update loja to kubelearn/loja:1.1 and record the reason in the Deployment’s kubernetes.io/change-cause annotation, with the text versao 1.1: carrinho novo (“version 1.1: new cart”).

Afterwards, kubectl rollout history deploy/loja shows the reason in the CHANGE-CAUSE column.
n2-change-cause.dica: metadata.annotations: { kubernetes.io/change-cause: "..." } (in quotes, because of the colon)
n2-change-cause.vidaReal: Writing in the renovation log why each one was done.
n2-change-cause.limite: The annotation is just text: nobody checks whether the reason is true.

n2-recreate.titulo: Full renovation: close everything and reopen
n2-recreate.enunciado: The report generator writes to a file that two versions can’t use at the same time. Update it to nginx:1.28 in a way that the old pods all leave before the new ones come in.
n2-recreate.vidaReal: A renovation that requires closing the whole floor: you can’t have the old plans and the new ones working together.
n2-recreate.limite: Closing everything has a price: during the switch, nobody is serving. Use it only when running both versions together breaks something.

testes.descricao: the two versions never ran together

n2-maxsurge.enunciado:
Today the loja app has 4 replicas and 1.1 needs to go in as fast as possible, without ever dropping below 4 ready pods.

Adjust the strategy to create all the new pods at once and only then remove the old ones, and switch the image.
n2-maxsurge.dica: maxSurge takes a number or a percentage: 100% of 4 is 4. And maxUnavailable: 0.
n2-maxsurge.vidaReal: Opening all the new apartments at once next to the old ones and only then closing the old ones: fast, but it needs spare room.
n2-maxsurge.limite: The extra room is real: for a while, the cluster has to fit twice the pods. In a tight cluster, the new ones would stay Pending.
n2-maxsurge.comoSaber: The switch happens in a few seconds and there are never fewer than 4 ready pods.

testes.descricao: within 5 seconds, the 4 new replicas are ready, with no gap
